reason: E3 supports ML-based yield strength prediction with quantified errors, and E1 supports DFT-based design of elastic properties, but none of the cited evidence addresses fracture toughness prediction, hierarchical heterostructures, or the claimed role of severe lattice distortion in enabling the surrogate model. The key premises about toughness and the specific HfNbTiVAl10 system are unsupported.
premises: ML surrogate models can predict yield strength of HEAs with ~11–13.5% error at 20–600°C
First-principles calculations can design lightweight HEAs with high specific stiffness
The D parameter (γsf/γusf) from first-principles predicts ductility in BCC HEAs
Severe lattice distortion promotes chemical short-range order that can be captured by mesoscale descriptors
Microstructural descriptors from imaging and DFT can be integrated into ML to predict toughness
